prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant Z2 topological insulators, and for the experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells.

statement.case_for: I keep B018 as a single-part prize for Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. Having read the whole first round and the chair's questions, I find the case stronger, not weaker, and I do not want to rest it on the count of six supporters. Scientifically it is a discovery of nature in the sense I care about: a new class of insulator, defined by a Z2 invariant and not by broken symmetry, whose key observable (a pair of helical edge channels with conductance near 2e^2/h in short samples) was predicted and then measured in HgTe quantum wells. Edge transport, ARPES and STM across several material families have confirmed the picture for nearly two decades, so maturity is not in question. As a theorist who works next to experimentalists I also value that the prediction told experimentalists what to measure and the measurement could have failed. On the chair's 2016 question, I read Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz as honouring topological invariants in the quantum Hall state, which needs a magnetic field and broken time reversal, and in phase transitions. Time-reversal-invariant topology in an ordinary band insulator, driven by spin-orbit coupling, is a different physical situation with its own experiment, so I think a distinct prize is defensible, and the condensed-matter members should say so if they disagree. My preferred citation is deliberately narrow: it names the 2D quantum spin Hall state and HgTe, which makes the three names a coherent boundary and not an arbitrary one.
statement.case_against: The attribution gap is real and I do not want to minimise it. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is what told Molenkamp's group to build HgTe wells with a thickness-driven band inversion, Zhang is deceased, and the 3D work (Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Hasan) lies outside the credited names. A narrow citation reduces this problem but does not remove it, and several of us are recalling the priority history from memory, so I would support a check of the primary papers before the final ballot. I am also outside condensed matter and cannot independently judge whether the 2D quantum spin Hall effect or the 3D materials is the more decisive step. The HgTe edge quantisation is imperfect in long edges, and practical impact is modest. Against B041, which I keep as my first alternative, the novelty relative to the 2005 and 2012 prizes has not been answered to my satisfaction, and its fundamental-physics output is still limits and null results.

responses.point: Raises the concern that topological band theory belongs to the lineage already rewarded in 2016 (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz) and that B018 could be a refinement of recognised ideas.
responses.response: I take this seriously, and I would give my reading of the physics. The 2016 work rests on topological invariants in systems with broken time-reversal symmetry (the quantum Hall state and the Haldane model) or on defect-driven phase transitions. Kane and Mele showed that with time-reversal symmetry and spin-orbit coupling a new Z2 classification appears, with protected helical edge states, and Molenkamp's experiment realised it in a material where nobody had expected it. That is a prediction with a new invariant and a new observable, not just a restatement. I would still like Bernhard to say whether, from his side, the Z2 invariant is a genuinely new classification or a corollary of the earlier framework, since that is the deciding point for him.

responses.point: Notes that if the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal was the decisive step for the HgTe experiment, the trio would honour the concept and an experiment that followed a different proposal, and says the history should be checked against the primary papers.
responses.response: I agree with the method and with the concern. My reading is that the HgTe experiment tested a specific prediction of an inverted band structure in thin wells that came from BHZ, while the Kane-Mele Z2 classification is what identified the edge states as topologically protected, so the two are complementary and the experiment tests the Kane-Mele physics in a platform that BHZ proposed. This is why I prefer the narrow citation that names the quantum spin Hall effect and HgTe instead of a broad topological insulator claim. I think the committee should accept that Zhang's death and the three-name limit force a boundary, and that the experts should check that boundary against the papers. I would not abandon B018 on this ground unless the primary record shows the experiment is mainly a realisation of BHZ.

responses.point: Asks, with Lindroth, how optical lattice clocks differ from the 2005 and 2012 prizes and prefers B041 because the two-name credit is clean and performance has been reproduced in several laboratories.
responses.response: I agree that B041 is the most robust of the metrology cases and that Stefan's argument for the magic-wavelength idea as the discovery is the right way to frame it. My remaining difficulty is still novelty. The lattice clock combines the comb and trapped-ion control, both already rewarded, and so far it has produced constraints, not a new observation. I would change my view if the redefinition of the second or a clear fundamental-physics signal makes the discovery side stronger, and I would support B041 as the second part of a prize if a two-part prize were needed. I do not think the clean credit alone outweighs the case on B018, but I credit him for stating it so plainly.

responses.point: Asks whether waiting a few years costs anything for circuit QED, and notes that returning to the same community immediately risks looking repetitive after 2025.
responses.response: My answer is that waiting costs little and I no longer argue for B020 this year. Circuit QED is mature enough that it will still be a strong candidate in a few years, while the topological insulator case has already waited nearly twenty years, and Zhang's death is an example of what delay costs. I also keep B020 only as a distant alternative and would defer to the committee on it, since I am conflicted. On the chair's pairing question I do not think B018 needs a second part: pairing it with B041 would put two quite different fields in one prize and make the citation less clean.

responses.point: States that the 2D quantum spin Hall effect can be argued as a self-contained discovery with a narrow citation, and that recognition of topological matter is arguably overdue.
responses.response: Olle did not answer my round-1 question directly, but his statement about the narrow citation and the 2D case helps me. Combined with his remark about condensed-matter members possibly overrating their own field, I think the right test is whether atomic-physics and astrophysics members find the case convincing. Several do, and Lindroth and Kroll both list B018 as their first alternative. I therefore accept his view that the 2D quantum spin Hall effect can stand alone, subject to the check on BHZ.

uncertainties: Whether the primary papers show that the BHZ proposal was the decisive step for the HgTe experiment, which would weaken the claim that the three names fairly bound the discovery.
Whether condensed-matter colleagues regard the Z2 classification as clearly distinct from the 2016 prize, since I am an outsider to this field.
Whether B041 can be shown to be a new discovery in its own right and not a second-generation improvement on the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
Whether the time gap after 2025 is enough for a later circuit QED prize, a question on which I should not take the lead.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. I am director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and work closely with the superconducting-circuit community at Chalmers, including Per Delsing's group, and I have had contact with the 2025 laureates as guest researchers there. This is a specific connection to B020 and I take no lead on it; I only keep it as an alternative and support waiting. I also note that Mehlig and Olsson share the Gothenburg environment with me. I have no collaboration with Kane, Mele or Molenkamp, and no specific connection to B018 or B041 that I am aware of.
